channel.title: How We Got Here: Lessons on Systemic Racism (female voice)
channel.description: Short, sourced lessons on how systemic racism was built in America, from the first slave laws to the weaponized 911 call, and what has worked to undo it. Every claim is labeled documented, debated, or belief or myth. Narrated by computer voices; full text, sources and quizzes at the link for each episode.
channel.itunes:author: Federal CAREN Act campaign

image.title: How We Got Here: Lessons on Systemic Racism (female voice)

item.title: 1. Before race: where the fear came from
item.description: There is no ancient secret. Race was built, mostly between 1450 and 1700, to justify taking land and people, and the fear behind it was fear of losing power. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=before-race&lang=en

item.title: 2. Columbus: what his own records say
item.description: What Columbus wrote about the Taíno, enslavement and tribute on Hispaniola, his arrest in chains, the records about Africans sailing west before him, and the myths on all sides. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=columbus&lang=en

item.title: 3. The colonizers: Portugal, Spain, Britain and the empire system
item.description: How Portugal opened the Atlantic slave trade, Spain debated whether Native people were human, Britain built the plantation law the U.S. inherited, and the United States became an empire itself. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=colonizers&lang=en

item.title: 4. The African diaspora in Latin America and the Caribbean
item.description: Most enslaved Africans were taken to the Caribbean and Latin America, not the U.S. Their story runs from Haiti and the 1937 Parsley massacre to Cuba, Mexico, Brazil's “racial democracy” and the 6 million Afro-Latinos in the U.S. today. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=afro-latino&lang=en

item.title: 5. Discovery and conquest
item.description: How the Doctrine of Discovery became U.S. law, and what it did to Native nations: war, removal, allotment and boarding schools, and the fight for sovereignty today. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=conquest&lang=en

item.title: 6. Native nations today: sovereignty, land and justice
item.description: More than 570 federally recognized tribal nations, treaties as “supreme law,” who can prosecute crimes on tribal land, child welfare, water, voting, and the return of land. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=sovereignty&lang=en

item.title: 7. Slavery makes race law
item.description: The Atlantic slave trade, the national economy it built, the laws that made slavery permanent and hereditary, and the people who resisted. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=slavery-law&lang=en

item.title: 8. Reconstruction overthrown
item.description: Freedom, citizenship and Black political power after the Civil War, and the terror, court rulings and laws that took them away. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=reconstruction&lang=en

item.title: 9. What we built: Black towns, institutions and self-determination
item.description: All-Black towns, banks, insurance companies, newspapers, churches and colleges built after slavery, often the very places that were later attacked. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=black-towns&lang=en

item.title: 10. Faith: used to oppress, used to liberate
item.description: How scripture justified slavery and how the Black church, abolitionists and people of many faiths turned it into a force for freedom. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=faith&lang=en

item.title: 11. Christian nationalism and race
item.description: What researchers mean by Christian nationalism, its history from the 1920s Klan to segregation academies, the debate over its link to racial attitudes, and the many Christians who oppose it. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=christian-nationalism&lang=en

item.title: 12. Black veterans: fighting for a country that fought them
item.description: From the Revolution to Vietnam: Black soldiers who fought abroad and were attacked at home, and how a veteran's blinding helped desegregate the military. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=veterans&lang=en

item.title: 13. Science as a weapon: medicine, eugenics and reproductive control
item.description: Scientific racism, medical experiments, and the forced sterilization of tens of thousands of Americans, plus what the evidence does and doesn't show about Planned Parenthood. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=science&lang=en

item.title: 14. Health: segregated care and false beliefs about bodies
item.description: Segregated hospitals, myths about pain and skin, race “corrections” in medical formulas, COVID, and the toll of living with racism. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=health&lang=en

item.title: 15. Borders: who gets to be American
item.description: “Free white persons,” Chinese Exclusion, racial quotas, mass deportations of Mexican Americans, Japanese American incarceration, and today's enforcement. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=borders&lang=en

item.title: 16. Immigration enforcement now
item.description: Local police acting as immigration agents, detention, racial profiling, sanctuary policies and the evidence about them, and what families can do. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=enforcement&lang=en

item.title: 17. Place: who gets to live where
item.description: Racial zoning, covenants, redlining, sundown towns, blockbusting and the Fair Housing Act, and why neighborhoods are still divided. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=place&lang=en

item.title: 18. Housing today: evictions, screening and keeping homes
item.description: Who gets evicted, tenant-screening algorithms, laws that punish tenants for calling 911, the homeownership gap, and tools that keep families housed. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=housing-today&lang=en

item.title: 19. Burned, flooded and taken: the communities America destroyed
item.description: Black Wall Street in Tulsa and dozens of other Black, Brown and immigrant communities that were burned, driven out, flooded, seized or bulldozed, plus how gentrification continues the pattern. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=destroyed&lang=en

item.title: 20. Schools: separate, unequal and still divided
item.description: Laws against reading, Rosenwald schools, Brown and the resistance to it, 38,000 Black educators pushed out, busing's limits, and unequal funding today. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=schools&lang=en

item.title: 21. Wealth: built, blocked and taken
item.description: Why the typical white family has about six times the wealth of the typical Black family: forty acres promised and taken back, a failed bank, New Deal and GI Bill exclusions, redlining, subprime lending, and how to rebuild. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=wealth&lang=en

item.title: 22. Labor: work, unions and the fight for fair pay
item.description: Sharecropping and debt peonage, unions that shut Black workers out and the ones that organized them, the Pullman porters, the 1941 march threat, the Memphis sanitation strike, and work today. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=labor&lang=en

item.title: 23. Banking, insurance and taxes
item.description: How mortgages, appraisals, insurance, property taxes and access to banks still cost Black and Latino families more today. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=banking&lang=en

item.title: 24. Environmental racism: who breathes the dirty air
item.description: Toxic waste, Cancer Alley, Flint, highways and heat: why polluting facilities cluster near Black, Latino and Native communities, and the movement that fought back. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=environment&lang=en

item.title: 25. The fight for the vote
item.description: How Black Americans won the vote, lost it to poll taxes, tests and terror, won it back in 1965, and are fighting for it again since the Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act in 2013. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=voting&lang=en

item.title: 26. Mass incarceration and the war on drugs
item.description: How the U.S. came to lock up more people than any other nation, why Black Americans are imprisoned at about five times the rate of white Americans, and what is starting to change. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=incarceration&lang=en

item.title: 27. Policing and the 911 call
item.description: From slave patrols and vagrancy laws to the weaponized 911 call, and what the data shows about who gets stopped and hurt. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=policing&lang=en

item.title: 28. Your rights with police, and after a weaponized call
item.description: What the law says you can and can't do when police stop you or come to your door, how to stay as safe as possible, and what to do afterward if someone called the police on you because of who you are. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=rights&lang=en

item.title: 29. Courts: juries, sentences and the death penalty
item.description: Who sits on juries, how race shapes charges and sentences, the death penalty case where statistics weren't enough, and the cost of not affording bail or a lawyer. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=courts&lang=en

item.title: 30. Watched: surveillance of Black and Brown communities
item.description: COINTELPRO's war on Dr. King and the Black Panthers, the killing of Fred Hampton, surveillance of Muslim neighborhoods, facial recognition errors, and the neighborhood app. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=surveillance&lang=en

item.title: 31. Technology and AI: old bias in new code
item.description: Risk scores in courtrooms, ads that skip Black users, gunshot sensors, hiring and health algorithms, and AI image generators: how technology can repeat discrimination, and how to make it accountable. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=technology&lang=en

item.title: 32. Media and image-making
item.description: From minstrel shows and The Birth of a Nation to “superpredators” and crime news, and the cameras that turned the story around. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=media&lang=en

item.title: 33. Many targets: Latino, Asian, Native and immigrant communities
item.description: Lynchings of Mexican Americans, Chinese expulsions and Japanese incarceration, anti-Asian violence, missing and murdered Indigenous women, and the moments these communities stood together. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=many-targets&lang=en

item.title: 34. The women who organized the movement
item.description: Ida B. Wells, Mary Church Terrell, Claudette Colvin, Ella Baker, Septima Clark, Diane Nash, Fannie Lou Hamer, and the women who founded Black Lives Matter. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=women&lang=en

item.title: 35. Sports, music and culture
item.description: Jack Johnson, Jackie Robinson and the Negro Leagues, athletes who protested, the Black roots of American music, and the debate over who profits from Black culture. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=culture&lang=en

item.title: 36. Black LGBTQ history
item.description: Bayard Rustin, who organized the March on Washington, the Harlem Renaissance, Stonewall, James Baldwin, Audre Lorde and Pauli Murray, and the violence facing Black trans women today. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=lgbtq&lang=en

item.title: 37. Systemic racism: how institutions carry it
item.description: What “systemic” and “institutional” racism mean, how neutral-sounding rules carry old discrimination forward, why the law usually demands proof of intent, and the honest debate about disparities. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=systemic&lang=en

item.title: 38. Is racism over? What the evidence shows today
item.description: Controlled experiments and large data studies from the last 15 years in housing, lending, policing, courts, medicine, child welfare and everyday life, and how to talk with someone who thinks racism is over. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=evidence&lang=en

item.title: 39. The 2020s: reckoning and backlash
item.description: Ahmaud Arbery, Breonna Taylor and George Floyd, the largest protests in U.S. history, the reforms that passed and the ones that didn't, and the backlash against teaching and addressing race. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=twenty-twenties&lang=en

item.title: 40. Equal or better: what the evidence shows
item.description: Identical résumés, unequal callbacks. Higher unemployment at every education level. And a long record of achievement against every barrier, which is the opposite of what the inferiority myth predicts. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=performance&lang=en

item.title: 41. A world system
item.description: Britain paying slaveholders, the partition of Africa, genocide in the Congo and Namibia, Nazi lawyers studying American race law, apartheid, and how other nations are reckoning. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=world&lang=en

item.title: 42. The global Black freedom struggle
item.description: From the Haitian Revolution to Pan-Africanism, Garvey, Négritude, African independence, the petition charging the U.S. with genocide, the anti-apartheid movement, and 2020's worldwide protests. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=global-freedom&lang=en

item.title: 43. How movements won, and the playbook for this one
item.description: The bus boycott, the legal campaign behind Brown, the sit-ins, Birmingham, Selma and the CAREN Act itself: what actually made them work, turned into a step-by-step plan. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=movements&lang=en

item.title: 44. How a bill becomes law, and how this one could
item.description: Introduction, committees, hearings, markup, the filibuster, the other chamber and the president, why most bills die, and a realistic path for a federal CAREN Act in the 120th Congress. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=lawmaking&lang=en

item.title: 45. Repair and reparations
item.description: What reparations means under international law, the precedents in the U.S. and abroad, Evanston, California and Tulsa, H.R. 40, and the honest arguments for and against. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=reparations&lang=en

item.title: 46. The path forward
item.description: What has actually worked, and where you fit in. https://prodataman.github.io/CAREN-Act/website/module.html?m=path-forward&lang=en
